topic: Present perfect with a referential past time adjunct
claim: The present perfect “is incompatible with referential temporal location in the past (see Ch. 3, §5.3): ∗I haven’t been to a party last Sunday.” The same page counts yesterday among the expressions that “always refer to a particular time”.
evidence_summary: The cited section states a default. Ch. 3, p. 143: “Except under conditions outlined below, time adjuncts like last week, two minutes ago, etc., which refer to times wholly before now, are incompatible with the present perfect”. Page 144 allows a past time adjunct “under restrictive conditions”, with the unmarked [13iia] We’ve already discussed it yesterday, and p. 145 says already “cancels the normally excluding effect of yesterday”.
finding: Chapter 8 states as categorical what its source states as a default, and the source’s exception uses yesterday, which Chapter 8 classes as always referential. The pointer to Ch. 3 carries the exception for a reader who follows it, but the sentence as printed is false by the book’s own example.
proposed_wording: This compound tense is normally incompatible with referential temporal location in the past
inference: Is the present perfect incompatible with a referential past time adjunct?

evidence.passage: §6.4, p. 699. “This compound tense is incompatible with referential temporal location in the past”.
evidence.example: Ch. 3, p. 144 [13iia] We’ve already discussed it yesterday, unmarked on the page image.
evidence.establishes: The cited section admits the combination under restrictive conditions.
